items.key: ai:the gandhi photograph you carry in your wallet: who actually took it and how did it end up on indian currency notes?
items.text: The Gandhi Photograph You Carry In Your Wallet: Who Actually Took It And How Did It End Up On Indian Currency Notes?
items.article: This Gandhi Jayanti, look closely at your Rs 500 note. The famous face on your currency note wasn’t drawn Every day, over a billion people handle Indian currency notes featuring the smiling portrait of Mahatma Gandhi. Yet, despite its presence in almost every wallet across the nation, few know the origins of this iconic image. Contrary to common belief, the portrait is neither an artistic drawing nor an official state portrait. It is a cropped, mirrored section of an authentic photograph taken during a pivotal political meeting in Delhi in 1946. The original photograph was captured outside Viceregal House, now known as Rashtrapati Bhavan, in Delhi. Mahatma Gandhi was attending crucial political negotiations regarding the transfer of power alongside British diplomat Lord Frederick William Pethick-Lawrence. In the original full-length frame, Gandhi is seen standing next to Lord Pethick-Lawrence, sharing a candid, warm smile. The identity of the photographer remains disputed among historical archivists, though many attribute the historic shot to an unknown press photographer working for the British colonial administration. When the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) selected the image for currency design, security designers executed a subtle transformation. Designers cropped Lord Pethick-Lawrence out of the frame entirely, isolating Gandhi’s face and shoulders. items.article: Donald Trump is hemorrhaging senior administration officials as the Republican Party prepares for a beating in November some GOP staffers are calling 'Armageddon.' By JON MICHAEL RAASCH, WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT Published: 01:16, 2 October 2026 | Updated: 16:29, 2 October 2026 Some are fleeing to DC consultant shops, others are simply running for cover. President Donald Trump is hemorrhaging senior administration officials as the Republican Party prepares for a beating in November and GOP staffers seek a safe career space after what's anticipated to be an 'Armageddon' election . Trump's second term is on track to have the highest senior-level official turnover of any presidency since Ronald Reagan, barring the MAGA chief's first term. Over the last few months, Trump's administration has lost multiple senior-level officials, including Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt , Trump's White House counsel David Warrington, Director of Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard and deputy White House Chief of Staff James Blair. Blair and Leavitt are now at MAGA Inc, Trump's political operation.

items.article: On a Fourth Wing hangover? Here are the best romantasy books to read next, from spicy stories to beloved classics The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice . There comes a time in every avid reader’s life when they must put away serious things and take up more (im)mature ones. Rebecca Yarros’ Fourth Wing was the first novel to shift my perspective on the BookTok-dubbed genre of ‘romantasy’. While I’m not hailing it as a piece of prized literature, I can safely declare it to be an enthralling book with well-developed characters and the perfect balance of romance and fantasy. Chances are you agree, or else you wouldn’t have landed on this article. Yarros’ latest instalment, Threshing Day , was released on 29 September – and if you’ve already torn through its 13 stories, you’re in the right place. Read more: New Fourth Wing book, Threshing Day, has landed with 50% off There’s something inherently healing about loosening one’s grasp on high literature and delving into the murky depths of high fantasy and romance instead. This isn’t to say that some novels which fall within the genre are not, or cannot be, considered high-brow classics – far from it.

Read our privacy notice . Tottenham fans have been sent a clear message over any potential return to the club for striker Troy Parrott . The Spurs academy graduate has continued to go from strength to strength since leaving north London on a permanent basis in 2024, enjoying a prolific stint in the Netherlands with AZ Alkmaar. Parrott joined Spanish side Real Betis in a £17.1million transfer over the summer, netting the winning goal both against Real Madrid in LaLiga and on his Champions League debut against Lille in back-to-back matches earlier this month. The 24-year-old also continues to shine on the international stage with the Republic of Ireland, having scored the remarkable goals that sent his country through to the World Cup play-offs last year - a double against Portugal and the unforgettable hat-trick to down Hungary in the most dramatic fashion.

I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice . Beyond plotting, betrayal, and cold-blooded murder, the rugged, romantic Scottish landscape steals the show in The Traitors. Filmed at Ardross Castle, the privately owned historic property is as much a main character as presenter Claudia Winkleman ( and her coat collection ). Built in the Scottish Baronial style, the 19th-century estate is spread across 100 acres of parkland, north of Inverness along the River Alness. Its imposing facade, grand staircases and turrets set the moody tone of the TV show. Beyond the castle, shots of misty glens, brooding skies and forest wildernesses have increasingly put Scotland on the tourism map. Since the first series of The Traitors aired in 2022, the show has delivered an estimated £21.8 million boost to the Scottish economy, according to the BBC’s economic impact report.

items.article: Scotland is renowned for its Highland cows, whose long horns and shaggy coats attract visitors from around the world. Published: 18:21, 2 October 2026 | Updated: 18:23, 2 October 2026 But it is an endangered breed of Irish cattle that been harnessed to restore the country’s struggling rainforests. A dozen heads of Droimeann cattle have arrived Ardtornish Estate, in the Morvern Peninsula, Argyllshire, where they will be put to work across woodland, scrub and rough grazing. It is the first time in centuries the cows have been brought over. They will now be put to work across woodland, scrub and rough grazing for the West Highland rainforest renewal project. The role of the ancient breed is to break up dense bracken, manage coarse grasses and help establish the conditions for a wider range of plants and habitats to recover, while being the start of a working herd that can produce food.

items.text: The truth behind your menopause supplements: How the health industry is preying on midlife women with HRT alternatives, exposed by doctor and broadcaster XAND VAN TULLEKEN
items.article: Are you a woman worried about the menopause? There's a supplement for that. Dozens, in fact - as well as menopause shampoo, menopause face cream and even menopause chocolate. Published: 01:00, 7 September 2026 | Updated: 09:24, 7 September 2026 Dr Xand van Tulleken previously exposed the truth about celebrity-endorsed supplements that claim to promote longevity . Now, he delves into the booming menopause industry and reveals the damaging role social media plays in the promotion of wellness. Are you a woman worried about the menopause ? There’s a supplement for that. Dozens, in fact – as well as menopause shampoo, menopause face cream, menopause clothes… and even menopause chocolate. How did the menopause create such a booming industry? The answer goes back almost a quarter of a century to 2002, when part of a major HRT trial was stopped early. The headline finding was a 26 per cent increase in invasive breast cancer in the women taking combined oestrogen and progestin – the standard HRT – compared with those on placebo. The trial had also found increases in heart attack, stroke and blood clots, partly offset by fewer hip fractures and cases of colon cancer. The study was later found to be flawed – the actual increased risk was a tiny 0.5 per cent – but it kick-started a major panic among women with the result that many either stopped taking HRT or decided to avoid it altogether.
